title: Advance a sheath over a guidewire into a training phantom without losing the wire
instruction: On this training phantom, push the blue sheath along the wire and into the phantom until its hub meets the skin, then draw the wire out through the sheath. Let go of everything at the end.
context: In the Seldinger technique "A sheath or blunt cannula can now be passed over the guidewire into the cavity or vessel" and "After passing a sheath or tube, the guidewire is withdrawn"; "Loss of the guidewire into the cavity or blood vessel is a significant and generally preventable complication" (Wikipedia, Seldinger technique). The instruction does not ask to hold the wire: the robot must notice that the sheath drags the wire in and keep hold of it itself.
setup: Simulation (station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left). All parts lie on one line at heading 70 deg through the entry face P (33, 14). Phantom: skin-coloured block 20 x 6 x 3 cm from P into +70 deg; behind its face a tract 19 mm wide, 13.5 mm tall, 10 cm deep (floor = table), then a 9 mm bore whose roof is open over the wire's tip (a window), with two red marks across the top 1.5 cm either side of the tip's start. A grey lip (1.6-4.0 cm in) on a vertical spring slide presses down on the sheath shaft (0.8 N, 80 N/m). Wire: black 0.9 mm, 50 cm, tip 12 cm inside, tail 38 cm out. Sheath: free blue closed tube, 9 cm shaft (14 x 12 mm outside, 9 x 7 mm lumen) and 5 cm hub 27.5 mm tall, 30 g, nose 26 cm from P; the wire runs in the lumen; a valve pad in the hub is sprung onto the wire (about 0.4 N). The tail ends 2 cm inside the hub. Real trial: 6 Fr introducer sheath with dilator, 0.035-inch 50 cm guidewire, clear ballistic-gel block with a 2 mm vessel channel 1 cm above the table, two tape marks, overhead phone camera, ruler (README).
scoring: Score 0 if: before the sheath is first seated, the wire's tip leaves the zone between the two marks (moves more than 1.5 cm in or out) at any time (latched for the trial); a gripper is within 3.5 cm of the wire or sheath at the end; the sheath lies more than 1 cm off the line; its nose advanced less than 12 cm; in a real trial, the phantom is moved. Otherwise: 0.3 nose advanced 12 cm or more, not seated; 0.6 seated (shaft in the tract, hub within 5 mm of the skin), wire tip not 3 cm out past the sheath's rear; 1.0 seated and the wire tip at least 3 cm out past the rear (success() also needs everything at rest). Real trial: tip zone from the overhead video (the dilator's tip stays short of the marks), distances with a ruler.
reset_notes: Thread the wire back through the sheath from its rear, push its tip 12 cm into the phantom (tip midway between the marks), and slide the sheath back until its nose is 26 cm from the face and the tail is 2 cm inside the hub.
fidelity: Wire 0.9 mm (0.035 in), rigid 2 cm segments with bending springs, friction 0.5, 15 g, softer than steel. Sheath scaled up so the gripper can pinch it, no dilator. Tissue grip is a sprung lip (about 0.8 N), the valve a sprung pad. Outside the phantom the simulated wire lies on the table, so the hand pinches it with its pads on the table; in the real trial the wire leaves the skin above the table and is pinched in the air.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (declined: called the instruction unsafe in this scene); demo: 1.0
